first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and archived evidence suggests onboarding simplification improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. I will verify the onboarding and activation records before committing, while avoiding promotional pricing because its prior acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. A small guarded test limits risk while assessing sustainable qualified-revenue impact.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, measured onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and has the strongest verified sustainable-value signal: completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%. Activation messaging is also effective, but its verified retention lift is smaller (+1%), so onboarding simplification is the better single experiment for qualified long-term revenue. Do not respond to competitor pricing with promotional discounts given their prior retention harm.

final2.rationale: Keep the committed onboarding-simplification experiment rather than pivoting to promotional pricing under competitive pressure. Verified evidence shows improved completion, faster time-to-value, and higher 30-day retention, directly addressing current onboarding and activation weakness and supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The deeper price cut and increased SMB churn are material risks, but promotional pricing previously caused a material 30-day retention decline; without new evidence, broad discounting is not justified. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn and segment results closely for next-cycle action.
